overview: This one-page Department of State “List of Papers” sheet indexes two items filed under telephone affairs relating to Japan, both dated November 29, 1940. The first records a telephone call concerning Japanese dollar bonds belonging to the Japanese affiliate of the International Telephone and Telegraph Corporation, which sought their prompt return to Japan aboard a Japanese steamer; it directs readers to file 894.51/675. The second notes information received about an increase in telephone rates in Shanghai. The sheet is an archival index rather than the underlying notes themselves.

subfiles.title: List of Papers concerning telephone affairs in Japan
subfiles.about: An index sheet describes two November 29, 1940 notes concerning the return of Japanese corporate bonds and an increase in Shanghai telephone rates.
subfiles.summary: The first indexed note reports Frank C. Page’s telephone call about Japanese dollar bonds of an International Telephone and Telegraph Corporation affiliate that were held by the parent corporation and requested for expedited shipment back to Japan by Japanese steamer. It cross-references the matter to decimal file 894.51/675. The second indexed note records information concerning increased telephone rates in Shanghai. The printed “10/12/45” on Form DS-46 appears to be a form designation or revision date rather than the date of the indexed records.

interest: The sheet is useful chiefly as a finding aid for records that may now be located elsewhere in the decimal files. Its juxtaposition of corporate securities, transpacific shipment, and Shanghai telephone pricing illustrates how the State Department’s telephone-related files could encompass both communications policy and the commercial affairs of telecommunications firms. The cross-reference to 894.51/675 offers a concrete trail for reconstructing the bond transaction and prewar U.S.-Japanese corporate relations.
